title: Zero-viscosity limit of the chemotaxis-Navier-Stokes equations with the Navier-slip boundary condition
summary: The interplay of chemotaxis and diffusion of nutrients or signaling chemicals in bacterial suspensions can produce a variety of structures with locally high concentrations of cells, including phyllotactic patterns, filaments, and concentrations in fabricated microstructures, which is described by the chemotaxis-Navier-Stokes flow by Tuval et al. in 2005.
